standard_prerequisites.name: The integral closure of a discrete valuation ring in a finite separable extension and multiplicativity of ramification indices
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the structure that lets the unramifiedness assumption be transported to a subextension.

standard_prerequisites.name: Unramifiedness with respect to A as etaleness of A -> B
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the hypothesis into a form to which permanence of etale ring maps applies.

standard_prerequisites.name: The normal closure as a Galois extension receiving a surjection from a tensor power
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the Galois extension required in part (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: Permanence of etale ring maps under tensor products, and etale extensions of a discrete valuation ring as products of Dedekind domains
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the step showing the tensor power is a product of Dedekind domains, from which unramifiedness follows.

core_obligations: Invoke the discussion of finite separable extensions and their integral closures without further mention (proof lines 33084-33086).

Part (1): let C/B/A be the integral closures; since C is finite over B the map Spec(C) -> Spec(B) is surjective, so for each maximal ideal m of B there is a maximal ideal m' of C above it (proof lines 33089-33093).

Part (1), conclusion: use multiplicativity of ramification indices and the unramifiedness hypothesis to get ramification index 1 for B_m over A, and deduce that kappa(m)/kappa_A is finite separable because kappa(m')/kappa_A is (proof lines 33094-33099).
Part (2): take M to be the normal closure of L over K, so M/K is Galois, and use the surjection from a tensor power L tensor_K ... tensor_K L onto M (proof lines 33102-33110).

Part (2), key step: note that unramifiedness of L with respect to A means A -> B is etale for B the integral closure, so by permanence of etale ring maps the tensor power B tensor_A ... tensor_A B is etale over A, hence a product of Dedekind domains, so M is the fraction field of a Dedekind domain finite etale over A and is therefore unramified (proof lines 33111-33127).
Part (3): with B_i the integral closure of A in L_i, argue as above to show B_1 tensor_A B_2 is finite etale over A; the author states that the details are omitted (proof lines 33130-33132).
difficulty_reason: The lemma has three parts for a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K: that in a tower M/L/K of finite separable extensions, if M is unramified with respect to A then so is L; that any unramified finite separable L/K is contained in a Galois M/K that is unramified; and that two unramified finite separable extensions are contained in a common unramified finite separable extension (source lines 33066-33081). Part (1) argues with the integral closures C/B/A: since C is finite over B, Spec(C) -> Spec(B) is surjective, so every maximal ideal m of B has a maximal ideal m' of C above it; multiplicativity of ramification indices together with the hypothesis gives that the ramification index of B_m over A is 1, and since kappa(m')/kappa_A is finite separable the same holds for kappa(m)/kappa_A (proof lines 33089-33099). Part (2) identifies 'L unramified with respect to A' with 'A -> B is etale' where B is the integral closure, takes M to be the normal closure of L over K, uses the surjection from a tensor power of L over K onto M, and applies permanence of etale maps to conclude that the tensor power of B over A is etale over A, hence a product of Dedekind domains, so M is unramified (proof lines 33102-33127). Part (3) is carried out 'in the same manner' and the author states that the details are omitted (proof lines 33130-33132). The non-routine content is the identification of unramifiedness with etaleness for the integral closure and the use of permanence of etale maps to reach the normal closure.
